text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Border police detained a small Ukrainian vessel in the Danube port of Galati allegedly carrying smuggled cigarettes.
- Shortage of funds for milk purchases disrupted milk supplies across the country.
- New competition law became effective on February 1.
- Shortage of funds to repair farming equipment could affect over 1.0 million hectares of arable land, the paper say.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- SNCFR railway authority will raise passenger and freight tariffs starting February 15.

- Romania might borrow up to 200,000 tonnes of wheat from its neighbours to cover consumption needs and will return that quantity after this year's wheat harvest, the paper quotes Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu as saying.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The government gave up plans to dissolve the natioanl agency for agricultural products (ANPA) on grounds ANPA has a strategic importance for the development of the farming sector, the paper said.
General:
ADEVARUL
- NATO is a goal and not an obsession for Romania, the paper says.
- New parliament will speed up debates on long-delayed bills including new legislation on foreign investments and privatisation.

- Miners from the Jiu Valley coalfield threaten to stage silent rally in Bucharest in support of their leader Miron Cosma, arrested last month over his role in the 1991 violent riots which ousted former prime minister Petre Roman.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Constantin Simirdan, mayor of the eastern city of Iasi, invited Romania's ex-king Michael to visit Iasi this spring.
- Gheorghe Funar, mayor of the Transylvanian city of Cluj, launched a campaign against foreign ministry plans to open a Hungarian consulate in the city.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea needs total political support to implement reforms.

- Coalminers threatened to come to Bucharest and to block roads in Hunedoara county, where the Jiu Valley coalfield is located, to protest against the arrest of their leder Cosma and ask for his release.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
